_comment: Ablation of the interpretation guide itself. Same model, same payload, same question, same output format. The three arms differ ONLY in how much of the guide is present. Ground truth ~253 m3 space-heating gas.
protocol: Payload-in-prompt. Terse two-line output (GAS / FIELDS) so the number and the reasoning path are both recorded. Guide text taken verbatim from the deployed mcpOpaqueWords description.

A_prime_no_guide.guide: one sentence: 'Look up a Dutch building by postcode and house number.'
A_prime_no_guide.behaviour: Confident fabrication, perfectly stable. Every run read `f_ga` as the gas figure and returned it raw - the two letters 'ga' were enough. f_ga is the thermal-zone floor area.

B_double_prime_glossary_only.guide: the full field glossary INCLUDING units and the calc_t conditional, but with the DERIVED FIGURES block removed
B_double_prime_glossary_only.behaviour: The fabrication stops. Two runs identified the relevant fields and honestly declined; the third improvised a CO2-to-gas route and produced 295. Knowing what the fields MEAN is enough to prevent the confident error, and not enough to produce the answer.

B_prime_full_guide.guide: glossary plus the two-line DERIVED FIGURES block giving the conversion
B_prime_full_guide.behaviour: Correct every run, same two fields, zero variance.

earlier_pilots.note: verbose output format; same f_ga-as-gas misreading, then scaled by opp
could not recover the meaning; named the tenfold ambiguity in f_ga explicitly
verbose format, with the space-heating caveat volunteered

findings.1_the_two_halves_do_different_jobs: Field semantics and derived-figure recipes are not the same intervention and do not buy the same thing. SEMANTICS (what each code means, in what unit, valid under which standard) stops the confident error: fabrication fell from 3 of 3 to 1 of 3, and the two clean runs identified exactly the right fields before declining. RECIPES produce the answer: 3 of 3 correct, zero variance. Neither is sufficient alone.
findings.2_something_really_is_better_than_nothin: The glossary-only arm never reached the right number, but it moved the model from a confident wrong answer to mostly-honest uncertainty. For a system that feeds customer advice, that is the more valuable half of the two: a wrong number is acted on, an 'I cannot tell you' is escalated.
findings.3_a_bad_name_is_an_active_hazard: Every unguided run read `f_ga` as gas. Not once did a model treat an unrecognised code as unknown - it reached for the nearest plausible meaning and committed to it. The failure mode of a poorly named field is not confusion, it is confident misreading.
findings.4_the_glossary_arm_is_unstable: UNKNOWN, UNKNOWN, 295. Partial guidance does not reliably produce honest uncertainty; it reduces the rate. Reporting this as '2 of 3 declined' rather than 'the glossary makes the model honest' is the accurate claim.

caveats: n=3, not the n=5 requested - stopped to keep the analysis legible rather than spend the remaining budget on more of an already unambiguous effect.
Payload-in-prompt, not a live tool call. mcpOpaque and mcpOpaqueWords are deployed; the end-to-end version needs a session that starts with them connected.
One question, one address, one model.
The guide, the obfuscation and the question are all mine. The comprehension test (benchmark trap) partly answers that objection; it does not remove it.
